source.snippet: In the Vivaldi web browser (which is based on Chromium), I want to capture screenshots of just the current viewport (not the entire page). I want to perform this action instantly via a keyboard shortcut. Surprisingly, Vivaldi does not seem to include a quick and frictionless way to accomplish this basic task without having to manually select the region to capture.

problem_statement: Knowledge workers and researchers using Chromium-based browsers (especially Vivaldi) have no fast, keyboard-shortcut-driven viewport screenshot tool — forcing slow manual region selection every time.
target_segment: Power users, researchers, and UX/product professionals who use Chromium-based browsers and need frequent screenshot capture as part of their workflow.
notes: Narrow but concrete pain. Comparable pain appeared in an HN thread (macOS screenshot tricks item in the batch, mentioning Skitch gaps on Linux). Screenshot tooling is a small but real paid category — Cleanshot X charges ~$30 one-time and has strong reviews. A cross-platform browser extension with one-key viewport capture could charge $5–15 one-time. Signal is single-source; strength kept at 2.
